webhook-id.meaning: unique message identifier; the same when the same webhook is resent after a failure

example_secret_note: the page's own example: use the part after whsec_ (5WbX5kEWLlfzsGNjH64I8lOOqUB6e8FH), base64 decoded, as the key
body_rule: the raw body, before any JSON parsing
steps: extract webhook-id, webhook-timestamp and webhook-signature from the headers
build the signed content: id, timestamp and raw body joined by periods
base64 decode the part of the secret after whsec_
HMAC the signed content with SHA-256 using the decoded secret, then base64 encode the result
extract all signatures from the webhook-signature header, removing version prefixes like v1,
compare the calculated signature to each provided signature with a constant-time comparison
verify the timestamp is within the acceptable tolerance (typically 5 minutes) to prevent replay attacks
success: if any signature matches and the timestamp is valid, the webhook is authentic
acknowledge: return any 2xx code to acknowledge receipt
